messages:
Micah: Heads up — saw a weird accounting spike for a customer request. They triggered a function/tool call mid-stream, then the client truncated the stream. Billing shows the toolcall tokens but the stream tokens are missing — or double-counted elsewhere. :thinking:

Ash: Can you paste the raw request/response IDs and router hop logs?

Micah: Paste below — request id 0x9f3a, router hops A -> B (fallback), toolcall invoked `fetch_kb` at ~t+120ms, client EOF at t+450ms. Billing trace: `toolcall: 324 tokens`, `stream: 0 tokens`, ledger later shows `stream: 312 tokens` attached to a different session id.

Micah: Logs (sanitized):
```
[6812349999] request=0x9f3a route=A->B fallback=true
[6812349950] toolcall id=tc-77 invoked fetch_kb tokens=324
[6812350100] client EOF, stream truncated, idle timeout
[6812350180] ledger: attach stream 312 tokens to session=0x7c11 (not 0x9f3a)
```

Jon: That smells like a routing handoff race. When we hand off to B we may be generating a new session token for the resumed stream and the ledger attribute path is losing the original request context. We should attach a stable "accounting_context_id" that survives route swaps/reconnects.

Tanya: Agree. If we add accounting_context_id at the edge and propagate it through the router/runtime, reconnections and retries can reconcile provisional credits to the original request. UX ask: console should show per-request waterfall with provisional vs confirmed credits + `route_origin` so SREs/customer success can see where the attach happened.

Ash: Two followups — (1) can we make it opt-in header for now so we don't change all clients? (2) any perf/size impact?

Jon: (1) yes, header `X-Accounting-Context` or `accounting_context_id` in metadata; runtime generates one if missing. (2) tiny — a 16B UUID per request, trivial for proto payloads. Bigger work is plumbing through the router and the ledger write path.

billing-bot: FYI current billing flow tags tokens with `session_id` and `provisional=true` until a final attach event. We don't currently carry `route_origin` nor a cross-hop stable id. That explains the orphaned stream tokens.

Micah: Nice. Any concerns about toolcalls being retried and double-billed? If a toolcall retries on timeout, we need the same accounting_context_id so we can dedupe.

Jon: Exactly. We should: 1) attach accounting_context_id to every child action (toolcall, embed job, background task), 2) ledger uses (accounting_context_id, sequence) for idempotency/dedupe.

Tanya: Console UX: propose a compact waterfall row per request showing: inbound tokens, toolcall tokens (per-tool name), provisional tokens, final attach event with diff. Also let users filter by `route_origin` (region/pool). This will cut down support loops.

Ash: Implementation plan? I can own the router plumbing. Jon you take ledger changes? Micah can you own the dashboard mockups with Tanya?

Jon: I can take ledger changes but need an API spec: how do we annotate writes? Suggest ledger write proto: `accounting_context_id` string, `dedupe_key` optional. We'll use `dedupe_key=toolcall_id` for toolcalls.

Micah: I'll produce a short repro and attach sample traces to the ticket. For support, can we add a temporary signal that surfaces orphaned tokens in the console (alert if provisional tokens > 0 after 5min)?

billing-bot: We can emit an alert signal called `provisional_aging` with tenant and request tags. Ops can mute for internal tests.

ops-bot: Temporary mitigation: add a router-side shim that copies the original `session_id` into `route_metadata.session_origin` on handoff. Not perfect, but cheap while we build accounting_context_id.

Tanya: Owner list confirmed: Ash/router, Jon/ledger, Micah+Tanya/console mock + repro, Billing team to own migrating billing pipeline tags. Can we sync tomorrow 10:30am?

Ash: Added to my calendar. I'll open the PR for router shim first.

Micah: Thanks — will post repro and customer impact note in the ticket. :thumbsup:
